sources._: Every value below is read from the file:line named here. Line numbers are emitted by the generator from the parsed source, not typed in, so they cannot drift silently.
sources.encoder: release/hardware/pcb/harness/contract_v4.json refs.RE1 = (6.025, 10.0) is the footprint ANCHOR (pin A), + release/hardware/case/v2/agentpad13_case_v2.py:367 offset (7.5, 2.5) = the SHAFT; cross-checks exactly against release/hardware/case/v2/agentpad13_case_v2.py:377. The plate opening is centred on the shaft, so this is the visible knob axis.
sources.plate_z: release/hardware/case/v2/agentpad13_case_v2.py:1152 and release/hardware/case/v2/agentpad13_case_v2.py:1153 = Z_PLATE_TOP - release/hardware/case/v2/agentpad13_case_v2.py:392. NOTE the trailing comment on that line still reads '# +3.5' from when PLATE_T was 1.5; the EVALUATED value is 3.4 and the shipped step/agentpad13_v2_plate.step measures z 3.4..5.0, which is what is published here.
sources.keycap_seat_z: 5.0 (deck, release/hardware/case/v2/agentpad13_case_v2.py:391) + 6.6 (stem shoulder above deck, release/hardware/case/v2/toppers/topper_frame_v2.py:79) - 0.0 (release/hardware/case/v2/toppers/topper_frame_v2.py:84) = 11.6, cross-checked against release/hardware/case/v2/toppers/topper_frame_v2.py:89. The shipped cap STLs are measured independently by the tests: their local z=0 is the bottom rim.

sources.stabilizer: release/hardware/pcb/harness/contract_v4.json refs.STAB1 (co-located with SW13) + release/hardware/case/v2/agentpad13_case_v2.py:609 / release/hardware/case/v2/agentpad13_case_v2.py:611, slot envelope release/hardware/case/v2/agentpad13_case_v2.py:610 (STAB_W, STAB_H = 6.65, 12.3)
sources.stab: The same slots as `stabilizer`, published as rectangles because the plate CUTS them: centres from release/hardware/case/v2/agentpad13_case_v2.py:609 / release/hardware/case/v2/agentpad13_case_v2.py:611 about contract refs.SW13, envelope from release/hardware/case/v2/agentpad13_case_v2.py:610. Independently confirmed by the fab gate's own readback in release/hardware/case/v2/CASE-V2-NOTES.md §14: '[SW13] cutout center (42.100,88.850) size 14.000x14.000 + stab L (30.162,89.47) / R (54.038,89.47) 6.65x12.3 UNCHANGED', and re-measured from the Edge.Cuts rectangles of the three shipped plate boards under release/hardware/case/v2/fab/ by the test suite.
sources.screws: MEASURED from the ORDERED boards: the four Ø3.2 Edge.Cuts circles present and identical in all three of release/hardware/case/v2/fab/agentpad13_v2_plate{,_tented_ring,_blank}_v5.kicad_pcb. Cross-checked against the case model's release/hardware/case/v2/agentpad13_case_v2.py:1277 (built on release/hardware/case/v2/agentpad13_case_v2.py:577) and release/hardware/case/v2/agentpad13_case_v2.py:592; the generator STOPs if the two disagree. Fastener envelope: release/hardware/case/v2/agentpad13_case_v2.py:602 / release/hardware/case/v2/agentpad13_case_v2.py:603 / release/hardware/case/v2/agentpad13_case_v2.py:601 / release/hardware/case/v2/agentpad13_case_v2.py:604, z from release/hardware/case/v2/agentpad13_case_v2.py:1291 and release/hardware/case/v2/agentpad13_case_v2.py:1292. NOTE the head is an ISO 7380 BUTTON head, not a socket-head cap: agentpad13_case_v2.py line 10 says the 'exposed M3 button heads sit PROUD on the deck'. A socket-head cap would be Ø5.5 x 3.0 and would not match the shipped counterbore-free plate. Also confirmed by the fab gate readback in the public CASE-V2-NOTES.md §14: 'screw holes Ø3.2 @ (3.7,3.7) and (80.5,3.7) present'.
sources.touch_pad: Centre from release/hardware/pcb/harness/contract_v4.json refs.TP5, restated at release/hardware/case/v2/agentpad13_case_v2.py:379. Every DIAMETER is measured off the ordered boards under release/hardware/case/v2/fab/: F.Cu electrode Ø14, B.Cu landing Ø14, B.Mask foam opening Ø8, and the per-variant marker -- Ø12 F.Mask opening (standard, the exposed ENIG gold disc) or Ø16 F.SilkS ring at 0.2 stroke (tented_ring) or nothing (blank). board_pour_mm is measured from the design polygon of the named TP5_touch / TOUCH_PAD zone in release/hardware/pcb/v5_7.kicad_pcb and cross-checked against contract refs.TP5.
sources.bases: Tilt from release/hardware/case/v2/bases/agentpad13_base.py:303 ((name, kind, tilt, body_thickness)), whose wedge/pedestal angle is the single constant release/hardware/case/v2/bases/agentpad13_base.py:276; riser 0.0, wedge 8.0, pedestal 8.0. Cross-checks release/hardware/case/v2/bases/params/agentpad13_base_params.json variants[].tilt_deg. The desk face is the plane in release/hardware/case/v2/bases/agentpad13_base.py desk_z(), lines 343-344, referenced to release/hardware/case/v2/bases/agentpad13_base.py:335 and release/hardware/case/v2/bases/agentpad13_base.py:129; plan silhouettes from release/hardware/case/v2/bases/agentpad13_base.py:169 / release/hardware/case/v2/bases/agentpad13_base.py:170 / release/hardware/case/v2/bases/agentpad13_base.py:171 (full-footprint) and release/hardware/case/v2/bases/agentpad13_base.py:208 (pedestal). Verified against the shipped STLs: riser z_min -12.500, wedge -26.994, pedestal -24.928. PARAMS-FILE DISAGREEMENT, recorded not fixed: that params file lists base_height_mm 17.49 for the PEDESTAL, which is the wedge's full-footprint figure inherited unchanged; the pedestal's own solid is 15.428 tall below the mating plane, because its Ø78 plan never reaches the far edge. height_mm here is the geometry-derived value and it matches the shipped STL.

Mating plane = the tray bottom release/hardware/case/v2/agentpad13_case_v2.py:1158

frame.name: board
frame.definition: The case model's xy board frame. Origin at the PCB's (0,0) corner; x -> physical RIGHT, y -> physical FRONT (toward the user), z -> UP with z = 0 at the PCB top face. Millimetres.
frame.handedness_source: release/hardware/case/v2/agentpad13_case_v2.py:1077 -- 'The design frame is LEFT-handed (x right, y DOWN from raw KiCad board coords, z up) while STL/STEP are right-handed, so every solid exported through this path is the ENANTIOMORPH of the intended part.'
orientation_facts: USB (J1) is at y = 3.05, the FAR edge away from the user -- release/hardware/case/v2/bases/INTERFACE.md:17 'The USB port is on the FAR edge, away from you.'
Encoder at x 13.525 (left of the x centreline 42.1) and stick at x 69.710 (right of it); board +x is 'the OWNER'S RIGHT' per agentpad13_case_v2.py:1597-1598.
Rendered as reality this reads: encoder BACK-LEFT, stick BACK-RIGHT, 2U key at the FRONT -- matching the TOP-DOWN panel of release/renders/v27_turntable.png.

to_gltf.note: Meshes in out/meshes/*.glb are ALREADY in glTF's Y-up right-handed space. To place a position from this file into that space use (X, Y, Z)_gltf = (x, z, y)_board. That swap has determinant -1, which is exactly what converts these left-handed board-frame numbers into the correctly handed real device; applying the usual det +1 Z-up->Y-up rotation (x, z, -y) instead would render the MIRROR IMAGE.

mesh_placement.note: 'baked' meshes already carry their assembly position in their vertex data -- load and add to the scene, no transform. 'instance' meshes sit at their own local origin and must be placed using the positions in this file.

instance.cap_*: place at (switch.x, keycap_seat_z, switch.y) in glTF space; cap local origin = centre of the bottom rim, +x along the 2U long axis (which is the board x axis for SW13)
instance.knob_*: place at (encoder.x, 0, encoder.y); the knob mesh already carries its absolute z (skirt bottom .. knob top)
instance.stick_cap_*: place at (stick.x, 0, stick.y); the cap mesh already carries its absolute z (14.4 .. 19.6)

stab.caveat: The plate slots are measured from every shipped plate board. release/hardware/case/v2/CASE-V2-NOTES.md §8 item 6 still requires coupon verification with the real 2U stabilizer; release/HOW-TO-ORDER.md §7 therefore tells stabilized builds to use the shipped 2u_stab cap.

screws.fastener: M3x8 ISO 7380 BUTTON head (NOT a socket-head cap)
screws.note: The head seats ON the plate top and stands proud: seat 5.0 -> head_top 6.8. There is no counterbore -- the plate hole is a plain Ø3.2 clearance.

bases.note: A base's flat top IS the tray bottom (mating_plane_z), so a base mesh needs no transform -- it is baked. What the viewer needs from here is the LEAN: rotate the whole device about the hinge line, which is the board-frame x axis at (y = hinge.y, z = hinge.z). The desk face is the plane z = desk_plane.ref_z - (desk_plane.ref_y - y) * slope_per_mm.
bases.tilt_axis: board x (the owner's LEFT-RIGHT axis). A tilt raises the FAR edge (y = 0, the USB / control-band edge away from the user) and leaves the NEAR edge (y = 100, the 2U key edge) down on the desk -- a back-raised typing wedge, agentpad13_base.py:69.
